title: Blow quality: a contact delivers harm by the work it can do (gate-08)
note: Ours, not the rules package's: every number here is ENGINE_SANDBOX until the rules package gives the form. The rules package's 'Almost no effective closing/cutting motion can still be a true contact, but should not automatically deal a full clean-cut injury or severance. Avoid hidden failure roll; require credible delivered work': 'one coherent gate-08 stage without double-counting tempo/Celerity or Melee. Very low-work glancing contacts can produce no cut without being turned into misses'. One stage, after the contact is admitted and before the pool is made whole: the damage potential (Strength's dice and the weapon's addend) times min(cap, Q^p), no roll. q = the contact's ImpactSpeed (the striking point's speed along the struck surface's normal) over its PeakSpeed (the swing's clip's own fastest tip speed at the rate it played): both scale with the swing's tempo, so Celerity's and Melee's tempo cancel. Q = q / q_ref, q_ref the blow's own median (references below), so a typical contact of every blow is Q = 1 and 1.1's quick and strong blows keep their identities. The switch blow-quality-off gives the earlier build's harm exactly; blow-quality-hilt-off the hilt alone.

form.source: the engine's proposal to the rules package (fifth return, section 5; the recommendation): p = 1 (momentum-like: the factor proportional to the speed into the surface; 2 would be energy-like), the factor at most 1.25 (a clean hit somewhat above a typical one, never a multiplier that makes speed the main road to harm), no floor beyond a pool of nothing (a low-work contact rolls a small pool and usually deals nothing: resisted by LowWork, never a miss). Potence's automatic successes unscaled (the rules package is asked whether they should scale).

hilt.source: ours (the rules package is asked): a contact of a blade's or a haft's class nearer the guard than a tenth of the blade (ContactMade.AlongBlade: 0 the guard, 1 the tip) is a bash with the hilt or the haft, not a cut: bashing harm (soaked as bashing, halved on a vampire), never a severance. The class's addend is kept (the quality factor already scales it: near the guard the blade moves slowly). The classes: rules/harm's lethal ones with a grip and a blade or head beyond it; not the claws or the fangs (no blade: AlongBlade 0 bare-handed), not the blunt (bashing already). Measured (the earlier build's matched duel): 7.4 % of the newly Embraced's body contacts met under 0.1, 11 % of his quick forehand's

cut_share.source: ours: severance's cut share re-based on Q (the rules package's bands measure the sine, which is inside q: the bands on top of Q would count the angle twice). A blow's band by its quality: Q at or above normal_from_quality takes rules/severance's normal share (1), at or above acute_from_quality its acute share (0.6), below it its glancing share (0: too little work ever cuts); Melee's edge on the normal and acute shares as for the angle's bands. The limits keep about the shares of contacts the angle's bands held: in the earlier build's matched duel the newly Embraced's body blows were 86 % normal, 13 % acute, 0.6 % glancing by the sine; by Q (his three clips' references) 83 % at or above 0.6, 16 % from 0.1, 1.2 % below 0.1 (blow-quality-strength.json, 2,402 contacts). A blow with no reference keeps the angle's band
